{{Short description|Mathematics research institute in France}}
[[File:Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques atrium.jpg|thumb|Atrium in the main building at the Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques in Luminy, Marseille, France.]]
The '''Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques''' ('''CIRM''') is a mathematics research institute associated with the [[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS) and the [[Société Mathématique de France]] (SMF). It is located in Luminy, [[Marseille]], France, and is affiliated with [[Aix-Marseille University]]. CIRM hosts weekly workshops on diverse topics where mathematicians and scientists from all over the world come to do collaborative research. Modeled as a "[[Medici villas|villa Medici]] of mathematics", it receives around 3,500 visitors per year.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Lis|first1=Louise|title=Dans la villa Médicis des maths|url=https://lejournal.cnrs.fr/articles/dans-la-villa-medicis-des-maths|website=Le journal|publisher=Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique|access-date=9 July 2017|language=fr|date=30 September 2015}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Luminy (4).jpg|thumb|CIRM Luminy residential hall]]
In 1954, a report from the CNRS discussed potential sites for a meeting place to hold international seminars and workshops in mathematics similar to the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Mathematisches Forschunginstitut Oberwolfach]]. The Luminy estate, formerly owned by the prominent [[Fabre Line|Fabre]] shipping family, was chosen in 1976.<ref>{{cite web|title=A Bit of History|url=https://www.cirm-math.com/a-bit-of-history.html|website=Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques|accessdate=9 July 2017}}</ref> The estate was handed over to the SMF in 1979. The center opened in 1981 and the first workshop was held in 1982.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Contrucci|first1=Jean|title=Le Centre international de rencontres mathématiques a été inauguré à Marseille|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1981/06/24/le-centre-international-de-rencontres-mathematiques-a-ete-inaugure-a-marseille_2729406_1819218.html|access-date=9 July 2017|work=Le Monde|date=24 June 1981|language=fr}}</ref>

==Scientific programs==
CIRM supports a variety of residential programs and workshops. Each year, CIRM runs around 35 week-long workshops with an average of 75 weekly participants.<ref>{{cite web|title=Propose an event|url=http://www.cirm-math.com/propose-an-event.html|website=Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques|access-date=9 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170725002101/http://www.cirm-math.com/propose-an-event.html|archive-date=25 July 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> CIRM also supports joint programs with [[Société de Mathématiques Appliquées et Industrielles]], [[Institut Henri Poincaré]], and [[Société Mathématique de France]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Le Centre d’Eté Mathématique de Recherche Avancée en Calcul Scientifique|url=http://smai.emath.fr/spip.php?article51&lang=fr|website=Societe de Mathematiques Appliquees et Industrielles|accessdate=9 July 2017|language=fr|date=24 October 2003}}</ref>

===Jean-Morlet Chair===
CIRM hosts the Jean-Morlet Chair, which is a six-month residential program for international researchers to collaborate with a local project leader from [[Aix-Marseille University]] to plan events and projects. The chair was named after [[Jean Morlet]], a French geophysicist who worked with Marseille-based researcher [[Alex Grossmann]], among others, to develop the [[wavelet transform]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Jean-Morlet Chair|url=http://www.chairejeanmorlet.com/|website=Chaire Jean-Morlet|publisher=Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques|accessdate=9 July 2017}}</ref> Past chairs have included Nicola Kistler, Boris Hasselblatt, Igor Shparlinski, [[Hans Georg Feichtinger]], Herwig Hauser, [[François Lalonde]], [[Dipendra Prasad]], [[Mariusz Lemańczyk]], [[Konstantin Khanin]], Shigeki Akiyama, and Genevieve Walsh.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Semester Chairs|url=https://www.chairejeanmorlet.com/semesters.html|website=Chaire Jean-Morlet|publisher=Centre International de Recontres Mathematiques|access-date=9 July 2017}}</ref>

*Robert Coquereaux: September 2000 – August 2005

*Patrick Foulon: September 2010 – August 2020
*Pascal Hubert: September 2020 – present
